presentMon.captureSemantics: 10 seconds to refocus, then 130 recorded seconds. Analyze 120 seconds after a predetermined 10-second measurement lead-in. The game must already be running; no process launch/input/injection is needed.
presentMon.schemaCaution: Corrected after real foreground smoke: CommandLine.cpp selects MilliSeconds by default. Default CLI headers include TimeInMs, CPUStartTimeInMs, MsBetweenAppStart, MsCPUBusy, MsGPUBusy. --v2_metrics emits CPUStartTime in milliseconds and FrameTime, not CPUFrameTime. The writer's seconds switch branch is not the parser-selected default. --qpc_time_ms uses CPUStartQPCTime milliseconds. CSV is UTF-8 with BOM.
presentMon.etwCaution: --track_etw_status is parsed in pinned CommandLine.cpp and prints counters through MainThread.cpp. New unified CSV does not contain those ETW columns; wrapper parses console counters and final loss warnings. Missing counters remain null, never assumed zero.
presentMon.method: Standalone ETW collection without an overlay or process injection; the service/MSI/GUI are unnecessary for this protocol.

gameCommandEvidence.safeRuntimeDiscovery: Use the game's ordinary console while out of a match: help cvarlist; help condump; cvarlist; condump. Prefer cvarlist <partial> for candidate families if full output exceeds console history. Identify the newly created condumpNNN.txt by timestamps; preserve existing output. Presence in a binary or old OptiLock list does not establish a currently writable release cvar.
gameCommandEvidence.launchDiscoveryCaution: Do not use -conclearlog as a default: it can erase an existing log, and its current build support was not established. +cvarlist is not a substitute for knowing when every client command has registered. Do not enable cheats or modify gameinfo.gi to make dev-only controls available.
gameCommandEvidence.profilerCaution: timedemo may run an accelerated replay and the built-in lite report may be session cumulative. Treat their syntax/functionality as candidates to verify, rather than substitutes for real-time ETW frametime distributions. Do not leave vprof active for FPS benchmarking.

protocol.preferredScenario: Native current-build match replay, fixed hero/player view and camera, playback speed 1, exact same tick range containing heavy combat. Use two distinct scenarios: representative lane/mid geometry and effect-heavy late fight. Record replay file hash, match identifier, start/end ticks, hero and camera mode.
protocol.fallback: Manually reproduce a timed Explore NYC route or native bot match with the same hero, team composition, difficulty, elapsed match time, purchases and camera landmarks. Bot AI and manual routing vary; do not market their averages as deterministic. No benchmark VPK/map, commands bypass, injected overlay or recorded gameplay input is needed.
protocol.warmup: After a game/driver update, restart into each candidate profile as required and traverse the full test interval at least twice before collecting warm runs. Retain shader caches. Keep first-run/cold stutter separate from warm throughput. Do not compare a cold renderer/profile against a previously warmed profile.
protocol.design: Three four-run blocks at minimum: A B B A, B A A B, A B B A. A = clean supported baseline, B = exactly specified candidate. Six captures per profile. Same 120-second effective route and fixed thermal/background conditions. Rewarm after shader/API changes; record all restart and cache states.
protocol.statistics: Per run: average FPS = 1000/mean frame interval; 1% low = 1000/mean largest ceil(N*0.01) intervals; separately report reciprocal p99, p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max frame time and >8.33/>16.67/>33.33ms counts. Keep genuine spikes. Independent unit is a four-run block, not individual correlated frames. No three-block confidence interval is claimed.
protocol.decision: Report all block gains and repeat variation. A candidate is only a consistent replay improvement when every block has positive average gain, median gain exceeds max(3%, observed within-profile repeat spread), 1% lows lose no more than 3%, and p99 worsens no more than 3%. This is a conservative engineering gate, not a statistical significance test or guarantee of live gains.
protocol.bottleneck: Use uncapped controlled captures for throughput. Compare native versus materially lower render resolution while other factors stay fixed. A strong FPS response and GPU-busy timing near the frame interval support a GPU limit; weak response suggests investigation of CPU simulation/render submission, memory, background work or caps. HAGS/Vulkan weaken GPU/CPU attribution, and total CPU utilization does not identify a single busy thread.
protocol.visualValidation: Compare the same scene/camera with native resolution and candidate downscaling/upscaling. Inspect distant silhouettes, soul orbs, fast target motion, ability warning shapes, haze, shadows, edges and UI text at normal play distance. Rank readable native and optional lower-quality profiles separately; visibility-destroying removals are not an accepted FPS win.
protocol.productionValidation: After selecting a replay candidate, validate bot and online play with current patch, including late-match effects and at least one 30-minute session. Verify cap/VRR/presentation behavior on the actual physical target display. FPS measurements do not establish full click-to-photon latency.

implementation.analyzeCommand: node optimization/tools/analyze-presentmon.mjs analyze capture.csv --metadata capture.json --profile PROFILE --run-id RUN --warmup 10 --duration 120 --out analysis.json

comparisonContextContract.matching: Entire comparisonContext matches exactly across reports, as do frame-time method, timestamp units, warmup, duration and collector version. Actual backend interventions need a separate explicitly designed context policy; never misstate renderer to force a comparison.
comparisonContextContract.evidenceLimit: Structural completeness validates declarations, not automatic runtime readback, scene state, matched camera or identical background activity.
